increments.title: Direct Mode is keyed to two observable cases
increments.goal: The session's rules and the README stop offering a judgement call as the test for Direct Mode and offer an observable predicate instead, with the price of taking it wrongly written down and every new rule guarded by a case in the repository suite.
criteria: `rulebook.md` keys Direct Mode to two observable cases: writing the issue file costs more than the change itself, and the loop cannot be run.
`rulebook.md` sends every task outside those two cases to Issue Mode.

`rulebook.md` states what taking Direct Mode for a task outside those two cases costs: the loop would have cut it `direct` and put a reviewer on the diff, and the session gives it no reviewer and spends the run's most expensive context on it.
`rulebook.md` quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation that price counters.
`rulebook.md` offers "small or obvious" nowhere as the test for Direct Mode.

`rulebook.md` keeps the rest of the Direct Mode section as it stands: read the code, change the code and the tests, run them, commit, push, open the pull request, and hand a broad search to a subagent.
`rulebook.md` keeps the mode-picking rule as it stands, including that an unanswered mode question falls to Issue Mode.
`test-repo.sh` has a case that turns red when `GEMINI.md` and `rulebook.md` differ.
Each rule this adds to `rulebook.md` gets a case in `test-repo.sh` that turns red when that rule is removed.
The paragraph in `README.md` that names the two modes states the same predicate as `rulebook.md` and states no other test.

return.plan:
GOAL
Replace the judgement call that opens Direct Mode in `rulebook.md` with a two-case predicate, write down the price of taking Direct Mode outside those cases, restate the same predicate in `README.md`, and guard every rule this adds with a case in `test-repo.sh`.

1. rulebook.md — rewrite ONLY the `### Direct Mode` section (lines 71-79 today).
Leave `## The two modes` (lines 32-42) and `### Issue Mode` (44-69) byte-for-byte as they stand; criterion 7 is satisfied by not touching them. Delete the sentence "Small or obvious work: you do it." The section becomes three paragraphs:

  P1, the predicate. Two cases and their concrete instances, then the fall-through. It must carry these strings verbatim, because the suite greps them: `the issue file costs more than the change` (case one, with its instance: a typo, one line in a document), `the loop cannot be run` (case two, with its instance: it is broken or not installed), and `Every other task goes to Issue Mode.`

  P2, the prohibition with its price and the quoted excuse. It must carry: a `Never take Direct Mode` prohibition covering tasks outside the two cases; the excuse quoted verbatim in plain ASCII double quotes, exactly `"this is too small to file an issue for"`; and the price, which names all four of `direct` in backticks (the loop would have cut that task `direct`), `reviewer on the diff`, `no reviewer`, and `most expensive context`. Form: this is the row-1 form of `.claude/rules/authoring.md` — a prohibition that carries its price and quotes the excuse it counters — and P1 is the row-4 form, a rule keyed to an observable predicate.

  P3, kept as it stands. The two surviving passages of today's section, unchanged apart from losing the opening judgement call: "Read the code, change the code and the tests, run them, commit, push, and make sure a pull request is open for the branch — the human merges it. No issue file, no researcher, no subagent is required." and "Hand a broad search through the code to a subagent anyway; it comes back as an answer instead of as a hundred files in your context."

  The phrase "small or obvious" must not survive anywhere in the file (criterion 5). The chosen excuse deliberately avoids both "obvious" and the pair "small or obvious" so the absence case cannot be tripped by the quote itself.

2. WORDS THE NEW TEXT MAY NOT CONTAIN. Existing cases in `test-repo.sh` own certain phrases and assert that `rulebook.md`, `README.md` and `GEMINI.md` do NOT carry them. Breaking one of these turns an unrelated case red:
  - `rationalisation` — test-repo.sh:2866 requires `.claude/rules/authoring.md` to be the only file carrying it. The acceptance criterion uses the word; the rulebook text must not. Write "the excuse" or quote the sentence directly.
  - `exemption clause` — test-repo.sh:2854, same ownership shape.
  - `occasion` (also matches "occasionally") — test-repo.sh:3061, same ownership shape.
  - `handoff` / `hand-off`, any spelling — test-repo.sh:343 scans rulebook.md and README.md. "Hand a broad search…" is fine; the compound word is not.
  - any agent page filename (`researcher.md`, `reviewer.md`, `planner.md`, `implementer.md`, `test-author.md`, `backlog.md`) — test-repo.sh:327 scans both files. Write "a reviewer", never the filename.
  - a sentence of the shape "nothing … agent/role … produced" without the word "break" — test-repo.sh:2434.
  GEMINI.md appears in those greps as its own path; because it is a symlink to rulebook.md, a banned word in the rulebook lights up two paths at once.

3. GEMINI.md — no change. It is already a symlink to `rulebook.md` (git mode 120000, `GEMINI.md -> rulebook.md`), so criterion 8 holds by construction. Do not replace it with a copy.

4. README.md — rewrite the two-mode sentence pair at lines 70-71, keep lines 72-73 (the `grill` sentence) as they stand. The new paragraph states the predicate and nothing else that could read as a second test: it drops "and you name which one", names Issue Mode as where every task goes, and names Direct Mode's two cases with the same two pinned strings as the rulebook — `the issue file costs more than the change` and `the loop cannot be run` — so one grep serves both files. Keep "no issue file, no subagents". The README stays a scannable overview: one short paragraph, no list.

5. test-repo.sh — append ONE new section, `echo "=== Direct Mode is keyed to two observable cases"`, immediately before the file's closing summary block (the final `echo` and `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]` at the end of the file, after case 16). Eight cases, listed in the test plan. Conventions of the file: `ok`/`no` helpers, one comment per case naming the criterion it covers and the production change that turns it red, section text extracted with `awk` the way the case at test-repo.sh:2488 extracts `### Issue Mode`. For `### Direct Mode` the extractor must exit on the next heading of any level (`^#{1,3} `), because the section is followed by `## The Human`, not by another `###`.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES
- A separate suite file for these cases: rejected. They are repository facts, which `test-repo.sh` already owns, and a new suite would need a line in `test.sh` and a doc of its own.
- Materialising `GEMINI.md` as a real copy plus a sync case: rejected. The symlink already makes divergence impossible; a copy would add a way to fail that does not exist today.
- Keeping "and you name which one" in the README: rejected. Criterion 11 allows the paragraph no test other than the predicate.
- Wording the price with the word "rationalisation", as the criterion does: rejected. It would turn test-repo.sh:2866 red.
- Touching `.claude/rules/authoring.md`, the agent pages or the `agent-brief` skill: out of scope. The issue says no agent picks a mode, and `authoring.md` is path-scoped to `skills/**` and `agents/**` — it guides this rewrite but is not bound by it.

return.testPlan:
WHETHER
Tests are needed. Every criterion but one is an assertion about the text of a file, and `test-repo.sh` is exactly the suite that owns assertions about this repository's own files.

WHERE THEY GO
All new cases go in one appended section of /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh, headed `echo "=== Direct Mode is keyed to two observable cases"`, placed immediately before the file's closing summary block (the final `echo` and `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]`), after case 16.

SUITE DOC
`test-repo.sh` has no suite doc and must not get one at the repository root: the case at test-repo.sh:176-180 turns red if a `CLAUDE.md` exists at the root, because it would load as project memory and be inherited by every subagent. The existing suite-doc case (test-repo.sh:2589) covers only directories holding `*.test.mjs`, so it does not ask for one here. Take the conventions from the file itself: `ok "<what holds>"` / `no "<what broke>"`, a comment above each case naming the criterion and the production change that turns it red, and section text extracted with `awk` as at test-repo.sh:2488. Do not create or edit any CLAUDE.md for this increment.

SECTION EXTRACTION
Two helpers the cases share:
  direct_section — awk over rulebook.md: start after `^### Direct Mode`, exit on the next `^#{1,3} ` heading (the following heading is `## The Human`, not a `###`).
  modes_section — awk over rulebook.md: start after `^## The two modes`, exit on the first `^### ` (that is the Issue Mode heading).
Grep the extracted text, not the whole file, wherever the case is about the Direct Mode section — a page-wide grep would pass on a phrase that survives somewhere else on the page.

WHAT — one case per criterion, every slot filled

1. `rulebook.md` keys Direct Mode to two observable cases — direct_section of rulebook.md → contains, case-insensitively, both `the issue file costs more than the change` and `the loop cannot be run` — break: delete either of the two case sentences from the Direct Mode section (each half asserted separately, so removing one case alone goes red).

2. `rulebook.md` sends every task outside those two cases to Issue Mode — direct_section of rulebook.md → contains `Every other task goes to Issue Mode` — break: delete that sentence, or soften it to "most other tasks".

3. `rulebook.md` states the price of taking Direct Mode outside the two cases — direct_section of rulebook.md → one paragraph carries all four of: a backticked `` `direct` ``, `reviewer on the diff`, `no reviewer`, `most expensive context` — break: delete the price clause, or drop the "no reviewer" half, or drop the "most expensive context" half; each alone goes red.

4. `rulebook.md` quotes, verbatim, the excuse that price counters — direct_section of rulebook.md → contains the exact ASCII-quoted string `"this is too small to file an issue for"`, quote marks included — break: replace the quoted excuse with an unquoted paraphrase, or drop the quote marks.

5. `rulebook.md` offers "small or obvious" nowhere as the test for Direct Mode — the whole of rulebook.md → no case-insensitive match for `small or obvious` — break: restore "Small or obvious work: you do it."

6. `rulebook.md` keeps the rest of the Direct Mode section — direct_section of rulebook.md → carries all of `Read the code`, `change the code and the tests`, `run them`, `commit`, `push`, `pull request`, and a sentence carrying both `broad search` and `subagent` — break: delete the "Read the code…" sentence, or delete the subagent-search paragraph; each alone goes red.

7. `rulebook.md` keeps the mode-picking rule as it stands — modes_section of rulebook.md → carries `The human names it` and `unanswered it falls to Issue Mode` — break: delete either sentence, or change the fall-through to Direct Mode.

8. `GEMINI.md` is byte-identical to `rulebook.md`, and 9. `test-repo.sh` has a case that turns red when they differ — the two files on disk → `cmp -s "$root/GEMINI.md" "$root/rulebook.md"` succeeds — break: replace the GEMINI.md symlink with a copy that carries one different byte, or delete GEMINI.md. One case covers both criteria: criterion 9 asks for the case, criterion 8 is what it asserts. The case comment should say that GEMINI.md is a symlink today, so the case is green by construction and exists to catch someone replacing it with a divergent file.

10. Each rule this adds to `rulebook.md` gets a case that turns red when that rule is removed — this criterion is discharged by cases 1-7 above: every rule the rewrite adds (the two cases, the fall-through, the price, the quoted excuse, the absence of the old judgement call) has exactly one case that names it, and every break listed above is a removal of that rule from rulebook.md. No extra case.

11. The `README.md` paragraph that names the two modes states the same predicate and no other test — the paragraph of README.md containing `Direct Mode` (extract the blank-line-delimited paragraph, or grep the file — the phrase occurs once) → contains both `the issue file costs more than the change` and `the loop cannot be run`, and README.md contains neither `small or obvious` nor `you name which one` — break: delete the predicate from the README paragraph, or restore "Two modes, and you name which one". Split into two cases, one positive (both markers present) and one negative (both stale tests absent), so either failure names itself.

12. `bash test.sh` exits 0 — the whole repository, unmodified working tree → exit 0 — break: any production change that turns a case in any suite red, the new cases above included. This criterion is discharged by running the command in the checks list, not by a new case.

HOW — every case
Cases 1-11: level integration (they read the real files on disk) — test file /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh — framework: plain bash with that file's own `ok`/`no` counters, no runner — command that runs just that file: `bash test-repo.sh` from /home/user/uroboros.
Criterion 12: level end-to-end — /home/user/uroboros/test.sh, not edited — framework: the same bash convention, one `run` line per suite — command: `bash test.sh` from /home/user/uroboros.

WATCH OUT WHEN WRITING THE CASES
The new case text lives in `test-repo.sh`, which is outside every phrase-ownership grep in the suite (those lists name agents/, skills/, .claude/rules/, rulebook.md, README.md and GEMINI.md only), so a case comment may quote the banned words freely. But the case at the end of the file (case 16) greps the whole repository for replaced sentences with `--exclude=test-repo.sh`; do not add "Small or obvious work: you do it." to any other file as a fixture.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE
A closed list, run from /home/user/uroboros, exit codes judge the work:
  bash test-repo.sh
  bash test.sh
Nothing else runs. There is no linter in this repository.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED
Nothing was run. No decision in this plan turns on a fact only a run can settle: the wording collisions were settled by reading the existing greps in test-repo.sh (lines 327, 343, 2434, 2854, 2866, 3061), and the tools the commands need were confirmed present. Both commands above are unrun as of this plan; the first run belongs to whoever runs them downstream.
